facts: All original _finish_streamed bytes preceding the wrapper are byte-identical between the two supplied revisions.
The child sets its own session, arms SIGKILL parent-death handling and checks that its original parent still exists before work; CPU90/AS1GiB/core0 and one-CPU affinity are actually read back.
The parent owns the exact child PID and receives real wait4 status and rusage. An outstanding child is killed and reaped in finally. The session-creation race has a direct PID kill fallback.
The parent does not claim success from child exit alone: it verifies the actual limit receipt/PIDs and reads both final JSON files before the first parent completion timing.

The final combined child+parent CPU and wall postcheck occurs after the process receipt write and flushed stdout. A failed final postcheck overwrites the process receipt as FAIL and raises, preserving the original child artifacts.
Original primary errors remain primary; subsequent kill/reap/save failures are recorded or added as notes rather than replacing the primary exception.
No target is rerun by this wrapper, and its separate budget cannot retroactively qualify the earlier166CPU sealing history.
budget_scope_qualification: A successful return is subject to the final measured aggregate90CPU/180wall gate. The child has asynchronous CPU/alarm enforcement and the parent supervises the child deadline. Parent metadata/stdout I/O after child reap has a post-completion gate, not a new asynchronous parent alarm; this review does not certify hard interruption of an indefinitely blocked parent write.
